instructions: Bring the broth and saffron to a boil in a small saucepan. Add the rice and 1/2 tsp of the salt, stir once and turn the heat to medium. Cook uncovered for 10 minutes, until there's very little liquid left.
Cover the pan, take it off the heat and let it sit for 5 minutes. The rice should be tender and a little sticky.

Meanwhile, pull the tentacles off the squid tubes and chop them small. Pat the tubes dry inside and out. Chop the onion fine and mince the garlic. Squeeze 1 tsp juice from the lemon, then cut the rest into wedges.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add half the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until soft. Add 2 of the garlic cloves and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped tentacles and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until they turn white and curl. Take the pan off the heat.
Stir in the cooked rice, 2 tbsp chopped parsley, the lemon juice and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Let it cool for a few minutes so you can handle it.
Fill each squid tube about three quarters full with the rice. Don't pack it, the rice swells as it cooks. Close each opening with a toothpick.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wide, deep pan over medium heat. Add the other half of the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until soft. Add the last 2 garlic cloves and the smoked paprika and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and add the pepper and the last 1/2 tsp of salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, until the sauce is thick.

While the sauce simmers, heat the last 2 tbsp of oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the stuffed squid for about 3 minutes, turning, until golden in spots. Don't pierce them. They'll spit hot juice.
Nestle the squid into the sauce. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 25 minutes, until a fork slides into a tube easily.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Take out the toothpicks and cut each tube into 3 pieces. Serve with the sauce spooned over, the rest of the parsley chopped over the top and the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Spain on a Fork leads (no rating shown): saffron rice, squid seared, a garlic, onion and smoked paprika tomato sauce, tubes stuffed with the rice and sliced. The squid's own chopped tentacles go into the filling, as in Food and Travel's version, and the squid then simmers in the sauce as in My Kitchen in Spain's. Pine nuts, ham and ground meat from those pages are left out. Chicken broth stands in for fish broth.
